answer: Make each identity commit a large block of unique pseudorandom data keyed to its own address, then prove retrievability each epoch by answering beacon-chosen spot reads — a proof of space, not of work. Verification is a falcon-quick check of a few delta offsets; generation and storage are not. Data keyed per address cannot be shared, so a thousand personas need a thousand independent committed stores held at once. One honest agent dedicates one disk; a farmer's cost in bytes scales linearly with headcount, no comet-tail of amortization across clones to hide behind.
